sites.evidence_type: N-terminal HA epitope; parallel surface-display screen
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface immunostaining PME 512.5 ± 62.2 (HA immunostaining, Tedman deep receptor scanning)
sites.rationale: Experimentally validated N-terminal HA epitope insertion (after signal-peptide cleavage where present); surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in Tedman et al. deep receptor scanning.

sources.citation: Tedman et al., Efficient experimental characterization of the GPCRome via deep receptor scanning, Nat Commun 2026 (bioRxiv 2025.09.19.677468, PMC12458215)
sources.claim: N-terminal HA epitope inserted per receptor; surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in a pooled GPCRome deep-receptor-scanning screen.

literature_notes: All four ledger lines (L1–L4) document C-terminal LgBiT fusions to Dr-GPR25 (zebrafish ortholog) expressed as full-length, membrane-anchored receptors in HEK293T cells. The C-terminus of GPR25 (residues 311–361) is intracellular per the topology landmarks, so these fusions are cytoplasmic tags and do not qualify as extracellular surface tag sites. The extracellular N-terminus (residues 1–39, no signal peptide), ECL1 (98–113), ECL2 (177–198), and ECL3 (268–287) are all topologically accessible surfaces, but no ledger line reports any insertion — epitope tag, fluorescent protein, transposon, or otherwise — at any of those positions. Per the rules, structural inference alone cannot ground a site; zero qualifying sites is the correct answer.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal LgBiT fusion to Dr-GPR25 (fish ortholog) is tolerated and supports β-arrestin recruitment, but residue 361 (W) is the last residue of the intracellular C-tail (topology 311–361 intracellular), making this a cytoplasmic tag site, not a surface tag site.
